memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph said to them, 'What is this you have done? Don't you know that a man like me can find things out by divination?'" — Gen 44:15 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph continues to speak as an Egyptian ruler would. But the question underneath his words is one every human being must eventually face: "What is this you have done?"

It is the same question God asked in the garden (Gen 3:13) and the same question He asked Cain (Gen 4:10). Not because God needed information, but because sinners need to be brought to the point of answering.

The brothers cannot answer. In a moment they will admit as much. And that is exactly where God wants every one of us — at the point where our explanations run out and we stop managing our own defence.

There is enormous relief in reaching that place. As long as we are defending ourselves, we cannot receive mercy; a person still arguing his case is not ready to accept a pardon. But when we finally say, "I have nothing to say for myself," the door to grace swings wide open.

The tax collector in Jesus' parable could not lift his eyes to heaven. All he could say was, "God, have mercy on me, a sinner." And Jesus said that man went home justified (Lk 18:13-14). Not the one with the good record. The one with no defence left.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you still managing a defence before God, or have you laid it down?
2. What is the hardest thing for you to admit before Him?
3. Why does grace only become real to us once our excuses run out?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: God, I stop defending myself. I have nothing to offer but my need. Have mercy on me, a sinner, and thank You that in Christ that prayer is always answered. Amen.
